question: During constant flux ultrafiltration, which trend most directly signals that fouling is building on the membrane surface?
correctAnswer: A steady rise in transmembrane pressure
explanation: At constant flux the membranes need more driving pressure as foulant accumulates, so transmembrane pressure climbs. Turbidity, temperature and setpoints do not show the fouling layer itself.
options: A steady rise in transmembrane pressure
A steady fall in permeate turbidity level
A steady rise in feed water temperature
A steady fall in backpulse frequency set
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Membrane Fouling and Cleaning. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: A steady rise in transmembrane pressure
optionB: A steady fall in permeate turbidity level
optionC: A steady rise in feed water temperature
optionD: A steady fall in backpulse frequency set

Rising turbidity in the treated water outlet

optionD: Rising turbidity in the treated water outlet
